task: Read CLAUDE.md, docs/history.md and all of src/ and test/ in this repository. Then write a plan, for my approval and not yet to be carried out, for rewriting the program in the Effect library (github.com/Effect-TS/effect). Target version 4: I have chosen full adoption of 4 over the stable 3.x so that we don't have to migrate from 3 to 4 soon afterwards. Check on npm whether 4.0 is final yet or still a release candidate, and pin the exact version, as the two SDKs are pinned. Full adoption means five things. (1) Effect Schema replaces src/schemas.ts and src/types.ts, so that one definition gives the type, the JSON Schema passed to Codex's outputSchema and to the Agent SDK's structured output, and runtime validation of every agent reply and every config and state file that is cast today. (2) Typed errors replace the single Halt class, and I/O and parse errors that now escape raw get their own error types. (3) Services and Layers replace the hand-passed Context record, and ScriptedUi, ScriptedPlanner and ScriptedReviewer become test layers. (4) Effect.gen is used throughout. (5) Interruption works: Ctrl+C aborts both SDK calls through their abort signals and closes readline cleanly. Verify every Effect API name and signature against the published .d.ts files of the chosen version, and every SDK option against node_modules, never from memory, because v4 differs from v3 and from most material online. In particular, prove early (as the first step of the plan) that the JSON Schema that Effect generates is accepted by Codex's strict structured output (additionalProperties: false, every property required) and by the Agent SDK, and say what the fallback is if it isn't. The rewrite must keep to the CLAUDE.md constraints: erasable syntax only, running directly under Node's type stripping with no build step, .ts import extensions, src/issueLog.ts pure, and src/claude.ts and src/codex.ts thin, with SDK callbacks such as canUseTool and hooks bridged back to Promises through a runtime. The nine decided behaviours must not change, and every existing scenario test must still cover the same behaviour after the rewrite. All development must be test-first, without exception. This is the most important requirement in this prompt and overrides convenience, speed and your own judgement. Before any application code is written or changed, write the tests that specify it. Run them and confirm that they fail, and that they fail for the reason the new code is meant to fix, not because of a typo or a missing import. Only then write the least application code that makes them pass. That includes restructuring whose current tests already pass: rewrite the tests into the new form first, and watch them fail. A step whose tests were written after its code, or never seen failing, has not been done and must be redone. The plan must name, for every step, the failing test that comes before it. Where code cannot be tested without credentials (src/claude.ts, src/codex.ts), move the logic into modules that the tests can reach. For any code that is left untestable, stop and ask me before writing it. Structure the plan as stages that each end with npm test passing and can each be committed on their own. List which CLAUDE.md rules and facts need rewording, including the dependency rule, which this change is my explicit permission to break for effect only. Ask me about any ambiguity, or any point where Effect's idioms conflict with a decided behaviour, rather than guessing.

questions.question: If the npm registry shows that effect 4.0 is not yet final (only a beta or release candidate under a 'next'/'beta' tag), should the plan pin that exact pre-release and go ahead, or should it stop until 4.0 is final?
questions.reason: You asked me to check npm and pin the exact version. I could not check: this planning call denies Bash and WebFetch ('only reading and writing under plan-review/ are permitted'), so neither `npm view effect dist-tags` nor the session-start `npm outdated` that CLAUDE.md requires could run. effect is also not in node_modules, so its .d.ts files cannot be read yet. The plan's first stage (pinning the version and reading the published .d.ts) depends on whether a pre-release is acceptable. Your choice of v4 over 3.x makes it likely that it is, but you have not said so for a beta, whose API may still change between releases.

proposed_answers.label: Pin the pre-release
proposed_answers.description: Pin the newest 4.0 beta or RC exactly (for example 4.0.0-beta.N), verify every API against that version's .d.ts files, and upgrade deliberately later, the same way as the SDKs.

proposed_answers.label: Pin only an RC or final
proposed_answers.description: Go ahead only if 4.0 is at least a release candidate. If it is still a beta, the plan stops at stage 0 and reports back.

proposed_answers.label: Wait for final
proposed_answers.description: Write the plan now, but carry it out only once 4.0.0 final is published.

questions.question: May the rewrite also depend on @effect/platform-node (NodeRuntime.runMain for SIGINT handling, plus the NodeFileSystem, Path and CommandExecutor services), or must it use the single `effect` package only?
questions.reason: You gave explicit permission to add 'effect only'. In Effect, the Node runtime entry point that turns SIGINT into fiber interruption, and the Node implementations of the FileSystem, Path and command services, live in the separate @effect/platform-node package (to be confirmed against the v4 .d.ts once the version is pinned). Without that package, src/main.ts needs its own process.on('SIGINT') handler that interrupts the main fiber, and src/state.ts keeps node:fs and execFileSync wrapped in Effect.try with typed errors. That choice decides the structure of the State/FileSystem service, the Ctrl+C mechanism and the dependency list. Neither package.json nor CLAUDE.md settles it.

proposed_answers.label: effect only
proposed_answers.description: No second package. A small SIGINT handler in main.ts interrupts the main fiber, and node:fs, readline and git calls are wrapped in Effect.try/tryPromise with our own tagged errors. The dependency rule is reworded for 'effect' only.

proposed_answers.label: Add @effect/platform-node
proposed_answers.description: Use NodeRuntime.runMain, NodeFileSystem and the command executor from the platform package, pinned to the exact version that matches effect. The dependency rule is reworded for both packages.

questions.question: What should Ctrl+C do after both SDK calls have been aborted and readline has been closed?
questions.reason: Today Ctrl+C kills the process with Node's default SIGINT handling. The finally block in src/main.ts does not run, so no session id or usage summary is printed, and nothing is written to conversation.md. With Effect interruption the finalizers do run, so the plan must say what they print and record and which exit code results. Decided behaviour 8 (records) and the 'HALTED ... State is preserved' output in main.ts touch this, but neither covers interruption. Each option needs its own scenario test (for example, interrupting while ScriptedUi is waiting for input, and while a scripted agent call is pending).

proposed_answers.label: Like a halt, exit 130
proposed_answers.description: Print 'INTERRUPTED by the user. State is preserved in …', append one line to conversation.md, print the Claude session id and the usage summary as a halt does, and exit with code 130.

proposed_answers.label: Same as 'q'
proposed_answers.description: Treat Ctrl+C exactly like answering 'q': the same 'HALTED: stopped by the user' output and exit code 1.

proposed_answers.label: Silent abort, exit 130
proposed_answers.description: Abort, close readline, print the session id and usage summary, and write nothing to conversation.md.

questions.question: When a config.json file (shared or per-project) fails Effect Schema validation, for example invalid JSON, a wrong type or an unknown key, should the run stop or carry on?
questions.reason: src/state.ts loadConfig currently spreads whatever JSON.parse returns over defaultConfig with a cast. An unknown or misspelled key is silently ignored, and a value of the wrong type goes straight into the run. Validating 'every config file that is cast today' (task point 1) requires a policy for failures, and decided behaviour 9 only fixes the precedence. Validating the known fields does not in itself require any change for unknown keys, so keeping today's silent tolerance is also possible. I have seen only the repository config.json, which has no stray key; I cannot see the per-project ones.

proposed_answers.label: Stop before any agent call
proposed_answers.description: A ConfigError names the file and the path of the failing field, and the run stops before state.init. Unknown keys are errors too, so a misspelled key cannot pass silently.

proposed_answers.label: Stop on wrong types, warn on unknown keys
proposed_answers.description: Invalid JSON and wrong types stop the run. Unknown keys produce a warning line in the terminal and are ignored.

proposed_answers.label: Stop on wrong types, ignore unknown keys
proposed_answers.description: Invalid JSON and wrong types stop the run. Unknown keys are ignored silently, as today, so existing config files keep working unchanged.

questions.question: When the structured reply of a planning, interview or review call fails schema validation (Claude Code's structured_output in a planning-mode call, or Codex's finalResponse), should the run stop with a typed error, or should the orchestrator send the agent one repair prompt with the decode error first?
questions.reason: Today src/claude.ts planning() casts structured_output without checking it, and src/codex.ts only checks that `issues` is an array before stopping. Validating every reply (task point 1) creates a new failure path. A repair turn would be new agent-facing behaviour that needs a new prompt in src/prompts.ts and new scenario tests, which is a decided-behaviour question I should not settle myself. Execution reports are not covered here: ClaudePlanner.executing() lets a recorded AskUserQuestion stop take precedence over a missing or failed report, and decided behaviour 4 requires revision and review before work continues. The plan therefore keeps this rule: a recorded stop wins over any validation failure, and an invalid execution report without a stop is treated like a missing one today (status 'aborted', the user is asked for input, then revision and review). There is never a halt or a repair turn inside the execution session.

proposed_answers.label: Stop with a typed error
proposed_answers.description: The reply is written to the round's JSON file for inspection, and the run stops with an AgentReplyInvalid error that includes Effect's formatted parse issue. No retry.

proposed_answers.label: One repair turn, then stop
proposed_answers.description: The same session or thread (never an execution session) gets a single prompt with the decode error. A second invalid reply stops the run. This needs a new prompt text and new tests.

questions.question: To keep src/claude.ts and src/codex.ts testable, may the SDK entry points (`query` from the Agent SDK and the `Codex` class, or its `startThread`/`run`) be injected as a service, so that tests supply fake message streams and threads, and only the two import lines that bind the real SDK stay untested?
questions.reason: You asked me to stop and ask before writing any code that stays untestable. Today, logic that the tests do not reach lives inside ClaudePlanner.call, including the message loop, usage recording, result/error mapping, the execution-stop logic and relayQuestions. test/claude.test.ts reaches the private denyAfterStop hook only through a cast. Two designs are possible. In one, the SDK functions become an injectable service and almost all of claude.ts and codex.ts is tested with fakes, including passing the AbortSignal (Options.abortController in the Agent SDK, TurnOptions.signal in the Codex SDK, which I found in node_modules/@openai/codex-sdk/dist/index.d.ts). In the other, the logic is extracted into pure modules and a thin untested adapter is left, which you would have to approve. This decides both the file layout and the list of untested code the plan must present to you.

proposed_answers.label: Inject the SDK functions
proposed_answers.description: A service interface holds `query` and a thread factory. The live layer binds the real SDKs in a few lines, which are the only untested code and are listed in the plan for your approval. Abort propagation, hooks and canUseTool bridging are tested with fakes.

proposed_answers.label: Extract pure logic only
proposed_answers.description: Message mapping, hook decisions and permission decisions move into pure modules that are tested directly. claude.ts and codex.ts remain thin adapters that call the SDKs directly, and they are untested. Each adapter is shown to you before it is written.

questions.question: The first step, proving that the JSON Schema Effect generates is accepted by Codex strict output and by the Agent SDK, needs real calls with credentials. Should the proof be a new prototype script or an extension of the existing prototypes, which you run in a project container while the plan waits for your result before stage 1?
questions.reason: The scripted tests can show that the generated schema has additionalProperties: false and every property required, and that its shape matches the current src/schemas.ts. Only a real Codex turn and a real Agent SDK call can show acceptance, however, and this development container has no project credentials for such a run (CLAUDE.md: prototypes run 'in a project container'). The gate is mandatory either way. The fallback is also derived from the Effect definition, so there is still a single definition: a pure, tested function that post-processes the generated JSON Schema (it forces additionalProperties: false and a complete required list, and inlines $defs/$ref). The prototype sends both the raw generated schema and the transformed one, so a single run shows which of the two is accepted. Only the placement of the proof is open.

proposed_answers.label: New prototype, plan waits
proposed_answers.description: Add prototypes/proto-schema.ts, which sends each generated schema and each transformed schema to one Codex turn and one Agent SDK call. You run it and report back. Stage 1 (Schema) starts only after one of the two is accepted by both agents.

proposed_answers.label: Extend existing prototypes
proposed_answers.description: Add the same two checks to prototypes/proto.ts and prototypes/proto-codex.ts instead of a new file. The gate is the same.

questions.question: Should effect be treated like the two SDKs in CLAUDE.md, with a check for newer versions at the start of every session and the same upgrade procedure, or only pinned and upgraded when you ask?
questions.reason: You asked me to list the CLAUDE.md rules that need rewording. The 'SDK versions' section names only the two SDKs and describes an upgrade procedure built around prototypes and real runs. Whether effect joins that stay-current policy, or stays frozen at the pinned v4 release, decides that wording. The docs do not settle it: you want the SDKs kept current, but you pinned effect to avoid migrations.

proposed_answers.label: Same policy as the SDKs
proposed_answers.description: Report newer effect versions at the start of each session. Upgrade by: bump the version, npm test, re-run the schema prototype, then one real run.

proposed_answers.label: Pinned, upgrade on request
proposed_answers.description: CLAUDE.md records effect's exact version and why it is pinned. It is upgraded only when you ask.
